item.title: Tesla recalls 12,000 vehicles over a seatbelt fault
item.description: Tesla, Inc. (NASDAQ: TSLA) said it would recall about 12,000 vehicles after a supplier shipped seatbelt anchors outside specification.
item.content:encoded:
No injuries have been reported, and dealers will replace the anchors at no cost.

Production at the Austin plant was not interrupted, the company said.

item.title: Apple beats March-quarter estimates on services strength
item.description: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) reported quarterly revenue of $96.4 billion, ahead of analyst estimates, as services growth offset softer iPhone sales.
item.content:encoded:
Shares rose 3 percent in extended trading after the results.

The company said gross margin held near 46 percent for the quarter.

Management guidance for the June quarter was broadly in line with consensus.

item.title: Wire One | After restoration, the Tesla museum in Belgrade reopens
item.description: The museum holds the inventor's notebooks and a working replica of his coil.
item.content:encoded:
The curator said the work took two years.

Letters between the inventor and Ford are shown in a new gallery from Friday.

Visitors can see the replica coil on the ground floor.

This report was produced by the newsroom's markets desk.

item.title: Apple opens flagship store in Mumbai
item.description: Apple said the site in Mumbai will open on March 14, the second it operates in the country.
item.content:encoded:
Staff have been training in Cupertino since December.

The building's owner said the fit-out took nine months.

item.title: Stocks close lower while investors weigh the rate path
item.description: The benchmark index closed 0.6 percent lower as investors weighed the outlook for interest rates.
item.content:encoded:
Among the movers, $AAPL, $AMZN and $TSLA fell, while $V, $F and $TGT edged higher.

This report was produced by the newsroom's markets desk.

item.title: FED SAYS ALL OPTIONS REMAIN OPEN ON RATES
item.description: The chair said the committee would decide meeting by meeting as inflation data arrive.
item.content:encoded:
Traders trimmed bets on a March cut after the remarks.

The statement kept the language on the balance sheet unchanged.

item.title: Amazon raises the price of Prime membership
item.description: Amazon.com, Inc. ($AMZN) said the annual Prime membership will cost $159 from May, the first increase in four years.
item.content:encoded:
Existing members will pay the new price at renewal.

The company said delivery speeds had improved in the past year.

item.title: Insect numbers are rebounding, an Amazon basin survey finds
item.description: Ecologists said larvae counts in the basin rose for a second season after years of decline.
item.content:encoded:
Caterpillar species tracked by the survey recovered fastest in protected habitat.

Deforestation in the Amazon basin slowed 8 percent, the survey said.

Shell fragments of river molluscs were counted along the same riverbank.

Conservation groups said the canopy is still thinner than in 2015.

This report was produced by the newsroom's markets desk.

item.title: Wire One | Visa fees rose for travellers on long stays
item.description: The consulate said the new schedule applies to applications filed after April 1.
item.content:encoded:
Tourists booking Amazon river cruises need the same documents, the consulate said.

Visa applications from students will be processed under the old fee, the embassy said.

This report was produced by the newsroom's markets desk.

item.title: Wire One | Premarket movers in software, energy and insurance
item.description: Analysts said margins held up better than feared across the sector as freight costs eased again.
item.content:encoded:
Volume in the premarket session was thin and few of the moves held into the open.

Among the movers, $ORCL, $SHEL and $GOOGL rose, while $META, $CAT and $ALL slipped.

This report was produced by the newsroom's markets desk.

item.title: Caterpillar and moth numbers rebound in northern woodlands
item.description: Surveys found larvae counts up by a third after two poor seasons.
item.content:encoded:
Warm springs favour the species that feed on birch.

Caterpillar damage was heaviest in the Apple orchards, the survey said.

Naturalists said butterflies followed the same trend.

item.title: Regulators weigh new rules for search advertising
item.description: The consultation covers disclosure, auction design and data sharing between services.
item.content:encoded:
Responses are due in June and a draft is expected in the autumn.

Analysts said Alphabet would carry the largest compliance burden in the market.

item.title: Home insurers repriced after the storm season
item.description: Filings in six states show average rate increases above 8 percent for homeowners.
item.content:encoded:
Brokers said Allstate filed the largest increases in two of those states.

Analysts said Allstate would keep tightening underwriting in coastal counties.

One broker said Allstate had slowed new business in Florida.

Renewal retention at Allstate held near 86 percent, the brokers said.

item.title: Wire One | Upgrade cycles for smartphones keep lengthening
item.description: Two carriers said the average replacement cycle has passed four years in their largest markets.
item.content:encoded:
Carriers said Apple has stretched that cycle furthest, trimming quarterly sales of new handsets.

Analysts at two firms said Apple would offset the slowdown with services revenue.

One supplier said Apple accounted for a fifth of its shipments last year.

Rivals have not matched Apple on trade pricing, the carriers said.

This report was produced by the newsroom's markets desk.

item.title: Wire One | A thin quarter is coming for European refiners
item.description: Refining margins in northwest Europe fell to the lowest level in two years.
item.content:encoded:
Traders said Shell had cut runs at two plants in response.

Analysts said Shell would lean on its trading business for the quarter.

One trader said Shell was buying fewer heavy barrels than usual.

Output at Shell facilities in the region fell 5 percent, traders said.

This report was produced by the newsroom's markets desk.

item.title: Apple growers brace for frost across the valley
item.description: Growers said an early frost damaged blossom across the valley and the harvest may fall by a fifth.
item.content:encoded:
Growers said Apple futures on the produce exchange rose 6 percent as buyers weighed a smaller crop.

Orchard owners have hired fewer seasonal workers than last year.

Caterpillar damage in the same orchards was lighter than last season.

The cooperative said cider makers would feel the shortage first.

item.title: Charging networks are opening to rival vehicles
item.description: Three operators said cross-brand access will be available at most sites by the summer.
item.content:encoded:
Operators said Tesla had opened the largest share of its connectors so far.

Analysts said Tesla earns a margin on every session sold to other brands.

One operator said Tesla hardware needed only a firmware change.

Drivers using Tesla connectors pay a small premium, the operators said.

This report was produced by the newsroom's markets desk.

item.title: City council approves the new transit line
item.description: The vote was nine to two after an hour of public comment on the chosen route.
item.content:encoded:
The authority said in a statement that the line will open in phases from 2029, with the first two stations serving the eastern district.

It said the cost estimate has not changed since the last review, and that federal funding covers about a third of the total.

A spokesperson said crews would begin work on the tunnel section in June.

item.title: Target lifts its same-store sales forecast
item.description: Target Corporation (NYSE: TGT) raised its same-store sales forecast after a strong quarter in grocery aisles.
item.content:encoded:
Shoppers made more trips than a year earlier, the retailer said.

Inventory was 4 percent lower at the end of the quarter.
